title: Token-slimming hedge + retry circuit for memory-safe continuous batching
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Intermittent OOMs during high-concurrency continuous batching workloads cause expensive full-request failures and long tail latency. Existing mitigations (aggressive eviction, global admission throttles, and fallback to smaller models) either regress quality or are too coarse-grained.

Proposal: Implement a request-level "token-slimming" hedging and retry circuit that combines three mechanisms: incremental prefix trimming guided by per-request fidelity hints, speculative micro-hedges to lightweight fallback decoders, and a coordinated retry circuit that preserves KV cache state and avoids duplicate heavy allocations. The system aims to reduce full request OOM rate, keep graceful degradation bounded to specific tokens/segments, and maintain high success rate for short/interactive latencies.
acceptance_criteria: OOM rate for P95 concurrent continuous-batching tests drops by >= 70% vs baseline on synthetic long-context workload
Median and P95 end-to-end latency for successful responses is not worse than baseline by more than 15% for non-trimmed requests
When token-slimming triggers, user-visible fidelity loss is constrained and observable via new fidelity tags in traces
No duplicate expensive KV materializations occur during hedge/retry within same request (verified by telemetry)
Feature flag gated rollout and automatic rollback path exists in runtime (config = token_slimming.enabled)
Automated e2e tests reproduce sequence: heavy-batch OOM -> token-slim trigger -> speculative micro-hedge -> retry succeeds without model swap
technical_notes:
Key idea: treat the KV cache as a shared, versioned resource and make retries idempotent with respect to expensive KV materialization. We implement three core components:

1) Prefix Trimmer: a lightweight transform that marks a request with a graded fidelity hint (full | relaxed | minimal). On memory pressure, the admission controller can request a 'relaxed' hint which trims non-essential prefixes (e.g., long system prompts, extended history beyond N tokens) before allocation. Trimmer exposes an API: trim_plan = runtime.trim_prefixes(request, budget_bytes).

2) Micro-Hedge Decoders: tiny, quantized micro-decoders (e.g., 2-3 layer decoder-only micro-models or distilled 1B variants) served as stateless hedges for immediate partial responses when main model allocation would OOM. They run in a lightweight class with strict token limits and do not allocate large KV objects.

3) Retry Circuit Manager: coordinates admission, keeps weak refs to KV materializations, and prevents double materialization. On OOM during allocation, the manager attempts: a) in-place prefix trim and retry; b) speculative micro-hedge for partial tokens while attempting a trimmed allocation; c) if trimmed allocation succeeds, merge hedge tokens into final output with provenance annotations. All operations are transactional from client's perspective and use idempotent request IDs.
implementation_plan: Design trim hint schema and integrate into SDK headers (design doc + example SDK patch)
Add runtime API hooks: trim_prefixes(), request_fidelity_hints, and weak-kvrefs in allocation path
Implement speculative micro-hedge worker pool and minimal model catalog entry (quantized micro-decoders)
Retry Circuit Manager: add finite-state machine (ALLOCATING -> OOM_HANDLED -> RETRYING -> SUCCESS/FAIL) with metrics and guardrails
Telemetry: emit events for trim decisions, hedge invocations, kv-materialization-ids, and retry outcomes
End-to-end integration tests in CI with synthetic long-context workload and golden assertions
testing_plan: Unit tests: trim_plan generation for varied prompt shapes and budgets
Integration tests: simulate allocation OOMs via memory-fault-injection and validate retry FSM paths
Load tests: run continuous-batching harness at 10x typical QPS with long-history prompts and assert OOM reduction per acceptance criteria
Quality regression: run existing evals on trimmed outputs and micro-hedge outputs, record delta in Rouge/BLEU and user-intent metrics
Chaos test: random KV eviction during retry to ensure weak-kvref semantics prevent double materialization
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 2% of traffic routed to a dedicated pool for 48h; monitor OOM rate, latency, fidelity tags
Ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% over sequential 48h windows if OOM reduction and latency targets met
Fallback: global disable via console toggle and automatic disable if OOM rate increases or CPU cost > threshold
Enterprise opt-out: Dedicated/Private customers can pin to legacy behavior for first 30 days
risks: Potential fidelity regressions for trimmed requests if trim heuristics are too aggressive
Complexity of merging micro-hedge token streams back into final response could introduce ordering or coherence bugs
Telemetry volume increase from fine-grained events; need aggregation before shipping to avoid costs
Incorrect weak-kvref lifecycle could leak memory or cause silent duplicate materializations
